chip_family.name: ARM
chip_family.description: 32-bit RISC CPU core family designed by Advanced RISC Machines (Arm) and licensed for embedding in third-party ASICs and systems-on-chip.

chip_family.name: MOS 6502
chip_family.description: MOS Technology 6502: low-cost 8-bit CPU family, widely second-sourced (Rockwell, Synertek, WDC), common as a low-cost main or sound CPU.

chip_family.name: Motorola 6800
chip_family.description: Motorola 6800: Motorola's first 8-bit microprocessor family, predecessor to the 6809.

chip_family.name: Motorola 6809
chip_family.description: Motorola 6809: 8-bit CPU with a more orthogonal instruction set and hardware multiply than the 6800; common as an arcade main or sound CPU in the early-to-mid 1980s.

chip_family.name: Motorola 68000
chip_family.description: 16/32-bit CISC CPUs (68000, 68010, 68020, ...) used as arcade and console main CPUs from the early 1980s onward.

chip_family.name: Intel MCS-48
chip_family.description: 8-bit single-chip microcomputer family (8048/8035/8039) with on-die program memory, typically used for I/O or protection duties rather than main game logic.

chip_family.name: Intel MCS-51
chip_family.description: 8-bit microcontroller family (8051 and its many second-sourced derivatives), successor to MCS-48, common in protection and peripheral roles.

chip_family.name: Yamaha OPL
chip_family.description: 2-operator FM synthesis family (YM3526/YM3812 and successors), later extended to 4-operator OPL3.

chip_family.name: Yamaha OPM
chip_family.description: Single-chip 4-operator/8-channel FM synthesizer family (YM2151) with no companion PSG or rhythm section.

chip_family.name: Yamaha OPN
chip_family.description: FM synthesis family (YM2203 and successors) pairing FM operators with an AY-3-8910-style PSG section.

chip_family.name: GI PSG
chip_family.description: The AY-3-8910 programmable sound generator family: three square-wave tone channels plus noise, second-sourced widely and cloned by Yamaha as the YM2149.

chip_family.name: Hitachi SuperH
chip_family.description: 32-bit RISC CPU family (SH-1/SH-2/SH-3/SH-4) used as the main processor of the Sega Saturn, 32X and Dreamcast generations.

chip_family.name: TMS320
chip_family.description: Programmable DSP family used in arcade hardware for audio synthesis and geometry/transform processing.

chip_family.name: Zilog Z80
chip_family.description: Zilog Z80: 8-bit CPU, a binary-compatible superset of the Intel 8080, ubiquitous as a sound or secondary CPU and common as a main CPU in lower-cost arcade boards.
